text:
eva: Heads-up — we just triaged a vuln in the deletion API. It looks like a recent RBAC change (PR #892) allowed a stale service role to call the /delete endpoint in some long-lived sessions. Not a wide blast but concerning for pending RTB/DAR requests.

mike: yikes. which environments? dev only or prod too?

eva: prod and staging. Exploit surface seems limited to requests routed through the legacy proxy (eu-region). We saw 3 anomalous delete ops in logs flagged by the monitor.

jon: can you paste the relevant logs or query? I want to see which principal did the calls.

eva: pasted query result (redacted):
```
2024-11-09T12:03:14Z allowed delete user=svc-legacy-proxy session=abcd1234 target=doc:xyz subject_request_id=SR-2024-1109-7
2024-11-09T12:04:02Z allowed delete user=svc-legacy-proxy session=abcd1234 target=doc:abc subject_request_id=SR-2024-1109-8
```

tara: are those subject_request IDs valid DSARs? we need to check legal holds. tagging @sasha-legal please advise on hold status for SR-2024-1109-*

sasha-legal: I checked — SR-2024-1109-7 is an active DSAR under review (not on legal hold). SR-2024-1109-8 was a requester-initiated delete (no hold). This is bad.

mike: immediate mitigation: can we gate deletes behind an authz check at the proxy (deny by default) and revoke svc-legacy-proxy role?

jon: we can push a config toggle: set PROXY_ALLOW_DELETE=false and roll the service account keys. Will deploy a safe rollback for 5m window.

ops-bot: deploy started: config-service/proxy toggle -> PROXY_ALLOW_DELETE=false (ci pipeline 2415013360)

jon: also rotate the KMS key used to sign service tokens for svc-legacy-proxy. Steps: 1) create new key version, 2) update token signer, 3) revoke old tokens. Example commands:
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=svc-token-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-prod
# revoke old tokens (example)
./authctl revoke --issuer svc-legacy-proxy --since 2024-11-09T00:00:00Z
```

eva: good. question: if those deletes already executed, what's our rollback/remediation for DSARs and retention exceptions? We need to know if we can restore documents from backups and whether KMS-integrated embeddings are affected.

sasha-legal: legal wants an evidence timeline and confirmation of erasure scope. If any data tied to an active DSAR was deleted, do not declare completion to the requester. We need to preserve evidence and follow Article 12/17 procedures.

mike: infra: snapshots exist for the object store with 24h retention. We can restore objects by timestamp. Not all derived artifacts (embeddings) are preserved in snapshots unless we ran snapshot-job-embeds daily. Need to verify.

jon: quick audit: run the search index for targets in the two SR IDs, then cross-check S3 object timestamps against snapshot manifest. I'll run now.

eva: also check audit logs for keystore/KMS requests around the same sessions — we need to see if keys were used to re-encrypt or sign anything. If the KMS key never exported plaintext, risk may be limited.

ops-bot: audit query complete: 3 KMS decrypt ops by key=projects/redwood/keys/embeds-key at 2024-11-09T12:02:58Z (requester svc-legacy-proxy)

mike: that suggests embeddings may have been accessed. We must assume some derived embeddings could have been re-generated or re-encrypted. Action items: stop further deletes, collect evidence snapshot, attempt object restore, and create temporary retention exception ticket in case restoration fails.

tara: can SRE/infra create a retention-exception ticket with severity=high and include a copy of the evidence? Legal will need that for notification and regulator reporting.

jon: creating ticket INF-RET-1123 with notes incl. snapshot IDs, affected SRs, KMS audit lines. ETA for initial restore probe 45m.

mike: also: audit-log retention must be frozen for the affected window — please set immutability flag and export logs to secure bucket.

ops-bot: export started: logs -> gs://redwood-sec-evidence/2415012345-export (job 9832)

eva: thanks. follow-ups: (1) postmortem draft started, (2) hold off DSAR completions, (3) coordinate a controlled restore + validation plan, (4) scope if embeddings need re-computation and deletion proof. I'll keep updates here. :point_up:

sasha-legal: confirmed — do not communicate erasure to requesters until legal OKs. Also prepare regulator notification if restoration cannot recover active DSAR data.

mike: timeline: 15m to config roll, 45m to initial restore probe, 2-3h for deeper forensics. We'll triage vuln PR and revert or harden RBAC checks to ensure least privilege.

jon: posting a short checklist for the next hour:
- revoke legacy service account keys
- toggle proxy delete flag (done)
- export and freeze audit logs (in progress)
- run object restore probe and verify checksums
- check embedding store snapshots and re-compute plan if needed
- create retention-exception ticket if restore fails

eva: perfect. I'll update incident channel and assign follow-ups. If anyone finds confirmed deleted active DSAR data that can't be restored, call legal and execs immediately.

ops-bot: incident status: mitigation applied, investigation ongoing.

mike: nits — we should add an automated check in CI to verify that new RBAC PRs don't reintroduce service-level delete grants. I'll open a follow-up issue.

jon: opened ENG-SEC-1244: add CI gate for authz matrix.

sasha-legal: thanks all. keep comms tight.

(End of thread)
